It maps closest to Sanderson's third method: raw hustle at massive scale.

Alpöge + Claude adapted Stepanov's function-field approach (multiplicity via determinants) to the integers by chaining ~√X theta lifts between unitary groups. Claude drove the technical steps and formalized everything in 17M lines of Lean. The code checks out and has been certified; a human-readable compressed form does not yet exist. A parallel pure-human GRH draft also appeared the same day.

Thus irrationality on the surface is actually a defense & coping mechanism underneath.

Starlink helped save a young man’s life in remote Myanmar.

After a landmine blast in Kayah State, his injuries were beyond what the medic on the ground could treat alone.

Using Starlink, the team sent photos and videos to a surgeon in Germany, who guided the medic through emergency procedures. Free Burma Rangers says this helped save his life and what remained of his leg.

For remote communities with no mobile signal, Starlink can put life-saving expertise within reach, even when the surgeon is thousands of miles away.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Out of everything posted about FSD v15 so far, one line from @elonmusk deserves way more attention than it's getting: "This is real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator. Let that sink in …" 🔥

Half of one accelerator is the part worth sitting with. Once you see the numbers behind it, Reality View stops looking like a fancy new screen and starts looking like one of the most impressive things Tesla has ever shipped.

🎬 THE SCREEN IS NOW GENERATED LIVE

For years, FSD's screen worked like a video game. Software took a list of what the car detected and dropped stock 3D models in the right spots: a gray car here, a lane line there.

Reality View tosses that playbook out the window. The car's AI now generates the video itself, frame after frame, as you drive, with no game engine anywhere in the loop.

Better yet, the picture comes from the same end-to-end model that's doing the driving. That's the single neural network that turns camera video into steering and braking, and now it paints your screen, too.

⚙️ WHAT A TRIP ACTUALLY IS

The standard AI4 computer carries two self-driving chips, and each chip packs three custom neural processors Tesla calls TRIP accelerators. That's six in all.

And that's where Reality View gets made: right on the self-driving computer, instead of the infotainment chip that runs your maps and music.

Each TRIP is basically an arena packed with tiny calculators, all cranking through the multiply-and-add math that neural networks run on. Teardowns count 9,216 of them per TRIP, lined up in a 96-by-96 grid and firing 2.2 billion times a second.

Each calculator handles two operations per tick, so one TRIP works out to 9,216 × 2 × 2.2 billion, or roughly 40 trillion operations every second.

Half of one comes to about 20 trillion, roughly a twelfth of the whole computer's neural muscle.

📏 WHY THAT NUMBER IS RIDICULOUS

Twenty trillion operations per second sounds enormous, until you see what else runs on that kind of budget.

The Neural Engine inside Apple's iPhone 15 Pro is rated at 35 trillion operations per second. So on paper, the slice of compute painting Reality View has less raw AI muscle than the AI chip in a 2023 phone.

Companies don't all count these numbers the same way, so it's a ballpark, but it shows just how little compute this is.

At the other end of the scale sits Nvidia's H100, one of the data-center workhorses powering today's AI boom. It's rated at about 1,979 trillion 8-bit operations per second in its standard mode, the same kind of math a TRIP runs, which puts half a TRIP at roughly 1% of one H100.

That gap matters because AI video is one of the toughest jobs in AI. Many AI video generators still take minutes to produce a single clip, as the researchers behind the real-time system MotionStream point out.

Even MotionStream, built specifically for speed, streams roughly 17 to 29 frames per second at 480p, and about 10 at 720p, while eating up an entire H100.

Meanwhile, Tesla is streaming a live, photorealistic view of the real road on roughly 1% of that chip's rated power, inside a moving car.

In other words, Reality View runs on less compute than a phone's AI chip, inside a computer whose main job is driving.

There's a fair asterisk here. Those research models dream up whole scenes from a prompt or a single image, while Tesla's renderer starts with a driving brain that already knows exactly what's around the car. Tesla also hasn't shared the view's resolution or frame rate.

And even on the most generous estimates of AI4's power, half a TRIP still works out to only about 2% of one H100.

Either way, live generated video on a sliver of a car computer would have sounded like science fiction not long ago.

🔍 HOW IT CAN BE THIS CHEAP

Tesla hasn't spelled out how it works, but it has left plenty of breadcrumbs.

FSD's network has been building its own 3D picture of the world for a while now, something Tesla showed off at the ICCV conference in October 2025. That picture includes 3D Gaussians, millions of soft little blobs of color that can rebuild a scene you can view from any angle.

Tesla also built its own Gaussian splatting system that can rebuild a scene from the car's cameras in a fraction of a second.

Reality View streams its picture from a virtual camera that can sit anywhere above the car, and showing a scene from an angle no real camera has is exactly what those 3D blobs are great at.

Even Elon seems to like that theory: he called a description of Reality View as a neural, Gaussian-splat digital twin "pretty accurate", and it lines up with every other clue.

If that's the trick, the hard part is done before the screen ever needs a picture. The driving brain understands the scene, and the visualization just paints what it already knows.

That would explain the other shocker. Reality View swapped every separate signal behind the old screen for one end-to-end visualization, and it still uses less compute than the bare-bones 2020 visualization did.

🚗 WHY TESLA CARES SO MUCH

v15 is Tesla's large model, built to squeeze every ounce of performance out of HW4. On a chip working that hard, a screen that costs half of one TRIP leaves nearly everything else for the driving.

And it's a flex, too. The AI4 computer costs about $650 by Elon's own figure, and that same box now drives the car and paints live video of the world at the same time.

This is only the start. Elon says Tesla vehicles will share traffic knowledge and combine it with Grok's real-time 𝕏 feed, even giving you a heads-up about what's happening at your destination.

A view this cheap to generate is the perfect canvas for that kind of shared knowledge.

Elon asked everyone to let that sink in, and the math earns it: half of one accelerator in a $650 computer is painting the real world live while FSD drives.

posts.text:
SpaceX is planning an absolutely massive 6-gigawatt supercomputing campus in Arizona, designed to operate with ZERO industrial water consumption

And the engineering behind this is absolutely insane

The proposed campus near Willcox includes:

• 747 acres of land
• Nine supercomputing buildings, each ~493,000 sq ft
• Up to 6 GW of electrical demand across four phases
• Up to 24 GWh of battery energy storage
• Dry cooling without conventional cooling towers
• ZERO industrial groundwater use under its proposed operating plan
• Just 7–10 acre-feet of estimated annual operational water consumption
• ~$3.6 BILLION in planned grid infrastructure upgrades
• ~1,000 permanent jobs and up to 5,500 construction workers

All of this is being planned in the middle of the Arizona desert

Building superintelligence infrastructure at this scale goes far beyond installing millions of GPUs

It means securing enormous amounts of electricity, building advanced cooling systems, expanding the power grid and solving engineering challenges that come with operating at gigawatt scale

A single 6 GW campus with 24 GWh of battery storage, designed to operate with minimal on-site water consumption

SpaceX is taking superintelligence infrastructure to an entirely different level

i'm admittedly pretty harsh on the google guys, mostly cuz i know the co super well.

but holy hell, i'm having an incredible time with neon so far.

product issues aside, this is a very different experience, almost like a strange new feeling. the way it talks, the way it responds, everything feels pretty damn fresh if that makes any sense. it's very creative. & unusually great at proposing ideas. i can't even say it's about intelligence or better answers in general. i am normally okay with words, but this is very difficult for me to articulate well.

anyway, it's fairly clear that google absolutely cooked here.

i have never doubted google's technical capabilities. those were & are totally obvious. i mean it is literally the birth place of ai. it was always a question of whether google could turn an extraordinary technology into newer experiences that ppl love using, which sort of requires shedding every success of the past.

these newer generation of models, particularly neon clearly gives them extraordinary new legs to stand on. it doesn't feel like "gemini" at all.

congratulations to everyone at google, i will continue to play around with more. there are obviously some product frustrations & confusing elements but i'm setting those aside for now.

posts.text:
Here is my initial FSD v15 review after driving with it all afternoon and evening:

First off, Elon was right. This update is a BANGER! Tesla Reality View is out of this world and so insanely cool I’m still trying to process it all. 

FSD V15.0.1 brings so many improvements behind the scenes, in addition to the wildly cool UI. 

Tesla Reality View IS AMAZING! Pictures and video don’t do it any justice, this is something that has to be experienced to truly understand. Got to take a few friends tonight on drives to show them and every single person was blown away by it. The amount of detail it shows and generates is wild and so impressive. It shows reflection in the car, buildings, trees, turn arrows on the display and more. 

FSD v15 now has pothole avoidance! I had it swerve and avoid/straddle a few potholes tonight that were difficult for me to see in the dark.

Another great new feature in FSD v15 is speed camera slowdown. As you approach a speed camera, it automatically slows smoothly to the speed limit if you are in a quicker profile. This is a huge quality of life improvement especially as more cities get speed cameras. 

Parking seems near unchanged from the last build, I feel it picking spots quicker especially at the supercharger I went to tonight. Seems to be preferring to park in the first or second open spot it sees which is great, but it tried to park in one handicap spot- otherwise good. By far, the coolest part is Tesla Reality View. Holy crap is it insane to watch while parking. It’s the best backup/360 camera money can buy and such a detailed and clear view. 

Another new change I haven’t seen many people talk about is the turn signal fade. On FSD, the turn signal sound gets quieter after a few clicks. This is so nice if you’re sitting at a red light and makes drives more peaceful. 

Quiet Mode is also so nice at night. It darkens the display and just shows arrival time; music, climate on the bottom and a quick grok button on the top. Another feature that makes it feel like a Robotaxi UI and a peaceful supervising experience.

Another improvement is much better handling of dips and speed bumps. The past couple updates it’s been a bit too fast in my Model Y, and it’s now so smooth.

The nag is definitely reduced. The last couple versions of v14.3 had been sometimes a bit strict, but definitely more relaxed in v15.0.1. Another thing I noticed is way less wiper washing, a very welcome change. 

Personalized parking preferences are SO cool. At home, I can click on a person icon on the map and choose street parking or driveway, and it backs into the driveway EXACTLY in the spot I park my Model Y. It leared where I park and knows it. 

It also now lets you choose which lot you want to park in if the mall or store has multiple lots, you can select it on the map, worked at the mall, Costco, and Home Depot tonight. 

I need to touch on Tesla Reality View again because it’s just that cool. It really feels like you’re in a video game like NFS or GTA. I’m blown away by this and didn’t expect it at all. quote.author: TeslaSI

quote.text:
Full release notes below

– – –  

v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:

Upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, which is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency, improving the critical intervention rate by 25x.

Introduced Tesla Reality View, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.

Improved navigation by using an end-to-end learned model based on route preference data from the fleet.

Improved parking location selection by using personalized parking history, and the map will now display multiple parking options at your destination.

Improved driver monitoring by increasing vision-based attention monitoring availability with hats and sunglasses and decreasing strictness in higher speed driver profiles.

Improved detection of road signs, small animals, road debris, and chains.

Improved detection of potholes, road details, and avoidance of deep standing water.

Improved speed handling for each driver profile, school zones and speed limits, and inclement weather.  

Improved Autoshift functionality by unifying with FSD-based gear predictions.

FSD V12 Introduced end-to-end neural-network driving.

FSD V13 built on that and reduced interventions.

• A new user interface that will re-render reality in a "mind-bending way."
• Fleet intelligence that incorporates driving information collected across Tesla vehicles.
• Voice integration, allowing drivers to request different routes conversationally (likely through Grok).
• Improved parking, destination handling and trip planning.
• 10x parameter count increase
• New lane change and exiting behavior
• And eventually (2027 for Model Y), FSD Unsupervised for personal cars (Tesla's robotaxis already run V15, and the personal Cybercabs being delivered next month likely will too).

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Flashback to June 14, 2024.

At the time, frontier AI models have zero fluid intelligence. They score around 5% on ARC 1. They can't reliably add two numbers. They make laughable logic errors every other prompt. Reasoning models don't exist. Coding agents don't exist. Claude Code doesn't exist. "Code gen" is a complete joke. Scaling up next-token prediction based on web text data is hitting a wall.

What if a time traveler told you that, by November 2026...

• AI models would have human-like fluid intelligence, thanks to a new paradigm: test-time induction (modern reasoning models).
• Not only would ARC 1 be saturated, but unreleased benchmarks 10x harder (ARC 2) and 100x harder (ARC 3) would be saturated too.
• Nearly all code would be written by AI, and models could one-shot complex codebases flawlessly.
• AI models would be solving multiple Millennium Prize problems.
• OpenAI's valuation would be 15x higher, and Anthropic's would be 85x higher.

And on top of all that...

• Nvidia would still hold ~80% of the AI compute market.
• Nvidia would have grown its revenue and earnings 4.5x.
• Nvidia would still be growing 75% a year.
• Nvidia would have even higher operating margins (67% vs. 65% back then).

Based on that information, straight from the future, would you have bought NVDA?

If you answered yes -- congrats. Today, 2.5 years later, you'd be down 5% on your investment (even more after inflation).

In the Chaco region alone, 95 schools have been connected, including schools serving Indigenous communities

Every installation undergoes a 60-item quality inspection, and even the antenna mounts are being manufactured by inmates trained through Paraguay's Ministry of Justice workshops

For thousands of children growing up in remote communities, this means access to online education, digital learning materials, and opportunities that were previously out of reach

This is exactly the kind of impact Starlink was built to deliver

Connecting places the rest of the internet infrastructure never reached

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
SpaceX is turning Starship production into something that looks more like a car factory than a traditional rocket factory

Inside Starfactory, SpaceX is now completing:

• 1 Starship upper stage every 2 weeks → ~26 per year
• 1 Super Heavy booster every 4 weeks → ~13 per year

And the scale of what's happening inside is insanely huge

• ~1 MILLION sq ft of manufacturing space
• ~330,000 sq ft of additional office space
• Rows of Starship nose cones numbered as high as Ship 51
• Multiple Starships and boosters being assembled simultaneously
• Most vehicles currently in production are intended to deploy Starlink V3 satellites

There's even a Starship nose cone with windows already cut into it, potentially being developed for NASA's Artemis lunar lander

And SpaceX is preparing to scale production even further

Each of the existing Mega Bays accommodates around 5–6 vehicle assemblies

The massive new ~700,000 sq ft Gigabay under construction at Starbase will have room for up to 24 vehicles simultaneously

That's an enormous expansion in SpaceX's ability to assemble and integrate Starships and Super Heavy boosters

The goal is to reach roughly ONE Starship launch every week beginning in 2027

What's especially impressive is that SpaceX isn't just designing the world's largest rocket anymore. It's also building the manufacturing infrastructure to produce these vehicles at an industrial scale

Starship is no longer just an experimental rocket. It has already moved into payload deployment, and SpaceX is now scaling toward mass production

We're watching that transformation happen inside Starfactory right now
